A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hessian-accelerated diffusion research and tilting-factor analysis, despite extensive retitling and reorganization. Their main text, mathematical material, tables, figures and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical convergence results and proofs, including its comparison table and appendices, but no original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v3 Section 5.1 and Figure 1 report original Gaussian-mixture sampling experiments comparing four samplers, averaged over 30 trials.

M1.justification: The exact Hessian-based sampler and Hessian-matching objective are retained. v3 adds the squared linear covariance approximation in Equation (11), allowing sampling without computing the original covariance matrix square root. This is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v3 adds one evaluated synthetic scenario: sampling a four-component Gaussian mixture in four dimensions. Gaussian mixtures were analyzed theoretically in v2, but were not empirically evaluated. The additional smoothness classes concern theoretical coverage, not new experimental tasks.

E2.justification: Within the new Gaussian-mixture experiment, v3 evaluates regular DDPM, the accelerated stochastic sampler of Gen Li et al. [14], and a PF-ODE sampler against its Hessian-based method. v2 has no empirical comparator set; its Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a numerical protocol estimating KL divergence with 200000 samples per trial, comparing sampling steps and trial computation time, and using Equation (12) with c = 4 and delta = 0.001. These are settings for one added experiment, not changes to an existing v2 evaluation.

E4.justification: Neither version reports distinct component ablations, sensitivity sweeps, distribution-shift tests or empirical error analyses. Figure 1 adds a comparative sampling experiment; the new covariance-perturbation guarantees are formal theoretical results.

E5.justification: v3 first reports averaging experimental performance over 30 trials. Figure 1 provides no error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 has no corresponding repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds the first numerical findings: the Hessian sampler has lower estimated KL at smaller step and time budgets; regular DDPM and the Li accelerator approach its level at larger budgets, while PF-ODE remains worse. These are new results from one synthetic study, not performance improvements over corresponding v2 measurements.

T1.justification: v3 removes the regular-sampler Theorems 1–4 and adds target-only Lipschitz-Hessian Theorem 4 with new arguments in Appendices G.4 and H.6. It also adds covariance-perturbation Corollaries 2–3, changes accelerated score-error control from fourth to second moments, explicitly assumes Hessian-estimator regularity, and changes the second-moment bound from M2 to M2d. Most earlier accelerated bounds remain; notably, v2 Theorem 6 becomes v3 Appendix G.3 Theorem 5.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift from guarantees for both regular and accelerated discrete-time samplers to accelerated DDPM over broader target distributions. Regular-sampler contributions disappear, while acceleration requiring Lipschitz Hessian smoothness only at q0 becomes a central new claim. Gaussian-mixture and finite-variance acceleration claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of score-accuracy requirements and sufficient Hessian-estimator regularity conditions in Section 4.1, matrix-square-root computational costs in Section 5.1, and why the target-only Hessian argument cannot directly use the discussed Poincare-based smoothness-preservation approach in Section 5.3.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the numerical study's dimension, component count, sample count and noise-schedule parameters, absent from v2. Reproducibility information remains limited: the experiment does not specify the complete mixture parameters, score/Hessian implementation, KL estimation procedure, hardware or code access.

R1.justification: Positioning changes from discrete-time versus discretized-SDE analysis to accelerated stochastic and ODE sampling under different target assumptions. v3 adds reverse-transition-kernel and sharp PF-ODE convergence references and explicitly acknowledges that its approximate sampler with the specified estimator coincides with Li et al. [13]. Much general related work is retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten. The accelerated method moves from Section 5 to Section 3, its analysis becomes the main organizing structure, and general related work and the full notation list move into appendices. Proof sections are substantially reorganized around acceleration.

P2.justification: Table 1 is restructured around accelerated stochastic and ODE guarantees, with revised groupings and captions. Its Gaussian-mixture row now displays N-dependence already present in v2's theorem. v3 adds the two-panel Figure 1 and changes the author block; the basic single-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a practical covariance approximation, initial numerical evidence and clearer positioning, while removing regular-sampler guarantees. However, its principal new theoretical extension relies on an unresolved step: Appendix H.6 applies Lemma 8's posterior third-moment identity to a remainder weighted by a derivative at mu_1^*(X1,X0), despite that factor also depending on X0. The supplied proof does not justify this substitution. This limits confidence in the main theoretical gain and prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
